standard: Access log of a transparent web and DNS filter (GW-SRV-PROXY-01); column names are plain
notes: All times UTC with a Z suffix. Sampling follows the Zeek logs: traffic that people cause is a 1-in-200 sample; machine-generated periodic traffic, sessions through the remote-access gateway and the employee VPN, and the flows behind an alert or an audit record are recorded in full. Allowed requests follow the Zeek flows; blocked requests and DNS-filter rows are complete. Hosts are joined by address to 06_data_streams/gw_host_registry.json. External addresses and names are invented. The filter sits in the path of outbound web traffic without changing addresses. For HTTPS it sees only the server name, not the path. A blocked request never reaches the internet, so it has no flow. DNS lookups are logged only when the filter has no category for the name (scheme dns); such a row carries the client, the name and the second of that lookup in dns.log. Byte counts are payload bytes, as orig_bytes / resp_bytes in conn.log. user: a name means that person was logged on to the client and the request was made in their session; requests made by the operating system, services and agents, requests from servers and all DNS rows carry '-'.

requests.description: One row per web request (per connection for HTTPS) or logged DNS lookup, in time order.

fields.name: time_utc
fields.notes: Request time: the second the flow started (the following second for a plain-HTTP request that falls just after a second boundary); for DNS rows the second of the lookup

fields.name: user
fields.notes: username in gw_host_registry.json users when the request was made in that person's logon session on the client; - for service, agent and operating-system traffic, for servers and for DNS rows

fields.name: method
fields.notes: CONNECT for HTTPS, the HTTP method for plain HTTP, QUERY for DNS

fields.name: host
fields.notes: Server name, or the address when the client gave no name

fields.name: status
fields.notes: HTTP status returned to the client (403 for blocked, 502/504 when the server did not answer); DNS response code (NOERROR, NXDOMAIN) for lookups

fields.name: category
fields.notes: Category the filter gives the destination; uncategorised when it has none; ip-address for a bare address

fields.name: bytes_in
fields.notes: Payload bytes to the client (the size of the block page for blocked requests)

fields.name: user_agent_family
fields.notes: For plain HTTP only: browser families and the families of update, certificate-check and agent clients; - for HTTPS and DNS
